parts.ms: M1 det(A − λI) or det(A − 2I) (or Ax = 2x); dM1 a² + 3a − 10 = 0 solved; A1. Printed (5) covers (b)(i) and (b)(ii) (MS p.14)

parts.ask: I_n = ∫cosⁿx dx: prove I_n = (1/n)cos^(n−1)x sin x + ((n − 1)/n)I_(n−2), n ≥ 2
parts.ms: M1 split cos x·cos^(n−1)x; dM1 parts to sin x cos^(n−1)x + ∫(n − 1)cos^(n−2)x sin²x dx; A1 sin²x = 1 − cos²x; A1* intermediate step, no missing arguments (MS p.20)
parts.er: Mostly good with the sensible split; chain rule on cos^(n−1)x was the usual failure; the Way 2 split led to abandoned work (ER p.5)

parts.ask: Show that for even n, ∫₀^(π/2) cosⁿx dx = ((n − 1)(n − 3)…3·1)/(n(n − 2)…4·2) × π/2
parts.ms: M1 I_n = ((n − 1)/n)I_(n−2) on [0, π/2]; A1 product form in I₀ after two applications; B1 I₀ = π/2 with evidence; A1* the boundary term shown to be 0 (MS p.20)
parts.er: Limited scoring: insufficient justification (how the formula gives the product, I₀ not shown, boundary term not shown to be 0); induction attempts mixed; many no response (ER p.5)

parts.ask: Hence find ∫₀^(π/2) cos⁶x sin²x dx exactly
parts.ms: M1 sin²x = 1 − cos²x, i.e. I₆ − I₈; A1 numerical expression; A1. Just "I = 5π/256" scores 0/3, but I₆ − I₈ = 5π/256 alone scores 3/3; no credit in (b) for work done in (c) (MS p.21)
parts.er: Reasonable source of marks; some re-applied the reduction formula instead of using (b) in this "Hence" part (ER p.5)

parts.ask: E: x² + 9y² = 9, foci F₁, F₂: their coordinates
parts.ms: M1 b² = a²(1 − e²) with a = 3, b = 1; A1 e; B1 foci as coordinates. Printed (4) covers (a)(i) and (a)(ii) (MS p.22)
parts.er: Errors extracting a and b; ±e penalised; a few used the hyperbola formula from Q2 (ER pp.5–6)

parts.ask: Equation of each directrix
parts.ms: B1ft (the scheme prints "(2)" against one B1ft mark; the printed (4) for (a) fixes it at 1). "a/e = 9√2/4" alone is B0 (MS p.22)
parts.er: Equations needed, not values of a/e (ER p.6)

parts.ask: P lies on E: show |PF₁| + |PF₂| = 6
parts.final_form: given result, valid for any P
parts.ms: M1 PF = e·PM (focus–directrix); dM1 PF₁ + PF₂ = e(M₁M₂) = e × 2a/e; A1*. Alts: constant-sum statement plus one point; parametric (3cos θ, sin θ) giving (3 − 2√2cos θ) + (3 + 2√2cos θ). "2a = 6" alone is 0/3 (MS pp.22–23)
parts.er: Discriminating: the eccentricity route was rare and often assumed PF₁ = PF₂; 2a = 6 alone insufficient; single points needed a constant-sum statement; parametric attempts could not take square roots of perfect squares (ER p.6)

parts.ask: Line y = 2x + c through P meets E again at Q; M is the midpoint of PQ: show the locus of M is a straight line through the origin
parts.final_form: y = −x/18, with the conclusion that it passes through O
parts.ms: M1 substitutes the line; A1 37x² + 36cx + 9c² − 9 = 0; dM1 x = ½(sum of roots) = −18c/37; A1; ddM1 eliminates c to x and y; A1* y = −x/18 with a conclusion (MS p.24)
parts.er: Only the most able scored; using half the sum of roots was not widely known; ±b/a or b/(2a) used for −b/(2a); many omitted the conclusion about the origin (ER p.6)

parts.ms: M1 at least two equations from TU = I (or UT = I), one correct; dM1 values for two unknowns; A1 two correct; A1 all three (MS pp.7–8)
parts.er: Mostly correct; errors in forming the matrix product; a few used UT = I, which gives simpler equations (ER p.4)

parts.ask: T maps l₁ to l₂: (x − 1)/3 = y/(−4) = z + 2; find a Cartesian equation of l₁
parts.ms: M1 l₂ as (1, 0, −2) + λ(3, −4, 1); M1 applies U (= T⁻¹) to position and direction (or solves Tx = point); dM1 converts to Cartesian; A1 (MS pp.9–10)
parts.er: Discriminated well: z + 2 wrongly given direction 0; many missed that T⁻¹ = U and recomputed it with errors; some used T instead of T⁻¹; many stopped at parametric form; the Tx = … route led to algebra trouble (ER p.4)

parts.ask: E: x²/49 + y²/b² = 1, 0 < b < 7, eccentricity e: write down the foci in terms of e
parts.ms: B1. Printed (2) covers (a)(i) and (a)(ii) (MS p.11)
parts.er: Widely correct; sometimes only one focus given (ER p.4)

parts.ask: Write down the directrices in terms of e
parts.ms: B1. Using 49 for 7 consistently in both scores B0B1 (MS p.11)
parts.er: Sometimes only one directrix, or "directrices =" instead of "x =" (ER p.4)

parts.ask: P(x, y) on E, x > 0; S the focus on the positive x-axis: PS² in terms of e, x, y
parts.ms: B1ft. Printed (2) covers (b)(i) and (b)(ii) (MS p.11)
parts.er: A few missed the y² term; some used PS = e·PM here, ignoring the required variables (ER p.4)

parts.ask: M on the directrix with PM parallel to the x-axis: PM² in terms of e and x
parts.ms: B1ft (MS p.11)
parts.er: Generally obtained (ER p.4)

parts.ask: Hence show b² = 49(1 − e²)
parts.final_form: given result, via x²(1 − e²) + y² = 49(1 − e²)
parts.ms: M1 PS² = e²PM² with their expressions, expanded; A1* all steps shown (MS p.11)
parts.er: Caused great confusion: very few progressed; many ignored (b) and reproduced a learnt derivation, forgot to square e, or used PS² = PM²; most abandoned (ER pp.4–5)

parts.ask: E meets the y-axis at (0, ±4√3): find e
parts.ms: M1 48 = 49(1 − e²) solved; A1 (MS p.11)
parts.er: Well understood but some kept ±1/7 and a surprising number chose the negative (ER p.5)

parts.ask: x-coordinate of P is 7/2: area of triangle OPM
parts.ms: M1 y = 6 from the ellipse; dM1 area ½ × (7/e − 7/2) × 6 (or shoelace); A1 exact. Using y² = 36 as y: M0M1A0 (MS p.12)
parts.er: Well answered; some used 36 not 6 for y; a few forgot to subtract 7/2 or subtracted a further triangle (ER p.5)

parts.ms: M1 Mx = λx (minimal working enough); A1; correct answer only scores both (MS p.13)
parts.er: Vast majority correct (ER p.5)

parts.ask: Given −3 is an eigenvalue, find a corresponding eigenvector
parts.ms: M1 (M + 3I)x = 0 solved, not all zero (or cross product of rows); A1 (MS p.13)
parts.er: Mostly correct; sign slips; some used 3 instead of −3 (ER p.5)

parts.ask: Given (1, 1, 1) is also an eigenvector, find diagonal D and orthogonal P with D = PᵀMP
parts.ms: B1 λ = 2; B1ft diagonal D with −3 and their values; M1 normalises an eigenvector; A1 consistent, labelled P and D (column directions may be reversed) (MS pp.13–14)

parts.ask: Using exponential definitions, prove 1 − sech²x ≡ tanh²x
parts.ms: B1 sech x (or tanh x) as exponentials; M1 single fraction, numerator expanded; A1* complete, numerators and denominators factorised; meet-in-the-middle needs a conclusion. Proving cosh² − sinh² = 1 then deducing is accepted (MS pp.15–16)
parts.er: Many lost a mark for insufficient working in a given result; using hyperbolic identities instead of exponentials scored nothing; meet-in-the-middle attempts often did not join up or lacked a conclusion (ER pp.5–6)

parts.ask: I_n = ∫ from 0 to (1/3)ln 2 of tanhⁿ3x dx: show I_n = I_(n−2) − pⁿ⁻¹/(3(n − 1)), n ≥ 2, find p
parts.ms: M1 tanhⁿ3x = tanh^(n−2)3x(1 − sech²3x) (sech²x for sech²3x not condoned unless recovered); dM1 ∫tanh^(n−2)3x sech²3x dx = tanh^(n−1)3x/(3(n − 1)); ddM1 introduces I_(n−2), tanh(ln 2) = 3/5 by exponentials (or calculator); A1 (MS p.17)
parts.er: Found difficult: most expected integration by parts, which led nowhere; many split as 1·tanhⁿ or tanh·tanh^(n−1) instead of using (a); the correct split gave a recognisable integral (ER p.6)

parts.ask: Hence find ∫ from 0 to (1/3)ln 2 of tanh⁵3x dx as a ln b + c, rational a, b, c
parts.ms: M1 reduction formula to I₅ in terms of I₁ (a made-up p allowed); M1 ∫tanh 3x dx = (1/3)ln cosh 3x; ddM1 cosh(ln 2) = 5/4, numerical I₅; A1 (c = −0.0708 accepted) (MS p.18)
parts.er: Marks available using the formula even without (b); I₁ was an obstacle and the 1/3 was sometimes lost; slips in c (ER p.6)

parts.ask: A(3, 2, 2), B(−1, 1, 3), C(−2, 4, 2): Cartesian equation of plane Π₁ through A, B, C
parts.ms: M1 two vectors in the plane by subtraction; dM1 cross product; ddM1 dot with a position vector; A1 any correct Cartesian equation (MS p.19)
parts.er: Often full marks; some left a vector equation; a few used position vectors instead of vectors in the plane and scored nothing (ER p.6)

parts.ask: D(−1, 1, −2); l through D perpendicular to Π₁ meets Π₂: r.(14i − j − 17k) = −66 at E: show DE = p√22
parts.ms: M1 line DE = D + λ(2, 5, 13); M1 substitutes into Π₂ and solves; A1 λ = 85/198; dM1 distance DE; A1. A fortuitous sign error in λ that still gives the right length scores M1M1A0M1A1ft (MS pp.20–21)
parts.er: Many coped well with λ = 85/198 despite non-integer values; algebra slips and wrong plane equations; most needlessly found E, increasing numerical slips (ER p.6)

parts.ask: F(4, 3, q): A, B, C, F form a tetrahedron of volume 12; find the possible q
parts.ms: M1 scalar triple product (linear in q); dM1 (1/6)(13q − 19) = ±12 solved; A1 both (MS p.21)
parts.er: Volume formula widely known; some forgot the 1/6 (lost 2 marks); many took only V = 12, not −12, so found one q (ER pp.6–7)

parts.ask: y = arccos(sech x), x > 0: show dy/dx = sech x
parts.ms: M1 derivative of the right form (chain rule or implicit via cos y = sech x); dM1 identities to x only, no roots (√tanh²x accepted); A1* two different hyperbolic functions seen before the answer; any sign error in d/dx arccos or d/dx sech is A0 (MS p.22)
parts.er: Progress by chain rule or implicit differentiation; some used wrong identities, made sign errors or gave too little justification (ER p.7)

parts.ask: f(x) = arccos(sech x) + coth x, x > 0, minimum at P: show its x-coordinate is ln(q + √q), q = ½(1 + √k), integer k
parts.ms: B1 d/dx coth x = −cosech²x; M1 sech x − cosech²x = 0 to a 3TQ in cosh x (or sech x, or a quartic in eˣ); A1 cosh²x − cosh x − 1 = 0; dM1 cosh x = (1 + √5)/2; ddM1 arcosh log form (or eˣ quadratic); A1. Writing the answer from cosh x without the log step: B1M1A1dM1ddM0A0 (MS pp.23–24)
parts.er: Identity from (a) often not used; −cosech²x mostly right but any sign error was costly; those working with eˣ stalled at the quartic; many wrote the given form without substituting into the arcosh log form (ER pp.3, 7)

parts.ask: C: y² = 8x, line l: x = 18 bound region R: show the perimeter of R is α + 2∫₀^β √(1 + y²/16) dy, find α, β
parts.ms: B1 dx/dy = y/4 (or dy/dx); M1 arc-length form in y with their derivative; A1 24 + 2∫₀¹²√(1 + y²/16) dy (MS p.25)
parts.er: Mostly correct; β = 18 seen; some used the surface-area formula; answers with no differentiation scored nothing (ER p.7)

parts.ask: Using y = 4sinh u and algebraic integration, find the exact perimeter in simplest form
parts.ms: B1 dy/du = 4cosh u; M1 full substitution; dM1 cosh²u = ½cosh 2u + ½ (or exponentials) integrated; A1; ddM1 upper limit arsinh 3 = ln(3 + √10), constants and lns only; A1 simplified exact. Calculator integration gets the first two marks at most (MS p.26)

parts.ask: M = (4 0 2; 0 4 a; 2 a 20/3); (1, 2, 3) is an eigenvector: find its eigenvalue
parts.ms: M1 top row times the vector suffices; A1 (MS pp.9–10)

parts.ask: Hence show that a = 4
parts.ms: M1 a correct equation in a from Mv = λv (e.g. 8 + 3a = 20); A1* from correct work (MS pp.9–10)

parts.ask: Find the other two eigenvalues; all working must be shown
parts.ms: M1 expansion of det(M − λI) must be seen (stating the factorised form is not enough); dM1 cubic = 0 solved (calculator allowed); A1 (MS pp.9–10)

parts.ask: Find a normalised eigenvector for each eigenvalue
parts.ms: M1 eigenvector equations set up and used (stated vectors without working is M0); A1 one new eigenvector (row vectors accepted); M1 normalises one; A1 both new ones normalised; B1 (1, 2, 3)/√14. The last 3 marks can be recovered in (e) (MS pp.9–10)

parts.ask: Hence find P and diagonal D with PᵀMP = D
parts.final_form: P has the normalised eigenvectors as columns; D = diag(10, 4, 2/3) in the matching order
parts.ms: B1ft P or D correct for theirs; B1ft both, matching order, no zero row/column; P and D swapped in labelling loses the second B (MS pp.9–10)

parts.ms: M1 dy/dx by parametric or implicit differentiation; A1 normal gradient (a sin θ)/(b cos θ); M1 line through P (y = mx + c must find c); A1* with an intermediate step (MS pp.16–17)
